title: Strict tower projection and exchange coefficient equations
statement: For the datum and chosen cartesian square with comparisons of [def-weil-pbc-ordered-coefficient-comparison-data], every derived-complete K satisfies three equalities in the actual derived strict tower category: the completed tower exchange is H inverse, followed by reduction of the ambient exchange, followed by H prime; restriction of H followed by beta equals rhoM followed by the constant H; restriction of the completed strict exchange followed by delta equals beta followed by the specified constant strict mate at reduction of Res K. These are the first three clauses of the original comparison, with no properness or finite-origin witnesses.

source.place: Second paragraph, specified conjugating maps; agent-supplied strict coefficient comparison supplement. Ingredient sources only: proetale.tex Tag 099M (lemma-naive-completion), Tag 099N (lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0A07 (lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim), Tag 0E48 (remark-compatible-with-diagram). None states this combined comparison.

proof.text:
the diagonal exact-adjunction comparison identifies the completed strict
exchange with the reduction of the ambient mate. The perfect quotient projection
maps are invertible, so conjugating gives the first formula. For the second,
transpose the projection formula map under the ordinary ringed adjunction.
Restriction identifies its counit with the constant counit, and quotient balancing
sends each pure tensor to the same tensor. Apply the derived pullback and tensor
comparison to this equation on the single strict quotient diagram. Tensor descent
makes it an equality of derived tower morphisms. For the third, transpose the
restricted strict exchange under the constant tower adjunction. Scalar restriction
identifies both units and counits, and coefficient inverse image respects
composition. The transpose is therefore the transpose defining the constant mate.
Bijectivity of the adjunction correspondence gives the equation. Naturality for
rho then gives exactly beta and delta at the reduced complete input. No claim of
faithfulness of derived evaluation functors is used.

lean.statement: theorem strictCoefficientEquations (sq : ChosenCartesianSquare g' f' f g) : ∀ (K : d.derived X) (hK : d.TowerComplete X K), (d.towerV' sq K = (exchangeRealizationH (f := f) (g := g) d K).inv ≫ (completedReductionTower Y' d).map ((d.integralExchange sq).app K) ≫ (exchangeRealizationHPrime (f' := f') (g' := g') d K).hom) ∧ ((exchangeTowerRes d Y').map (exchangeRealizationH (f := f) (g := g) d K).hom ≫ (beta (f := f) (g := g) d K).hom = (rhoM (f := f) (g := g) d K).hom ≫ (H (f := f) (g := g) d ((res d X).obj K)).hom) ∧ ((exchangeTowerRes d Y').map (d.towerV' sq K) ≫ (delta (f' := f') (g' := g') d K).hom = (beta (f := f) (g := g) d K).hom ≫ (exchangeConstantSquare (A := A) sq).exchangeTowerMate.app ((reduction d X).obj ((res d X).obj K)))
